articleTitle: Typhoon HIL Real-Time Validation of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor’s Control
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents the validation of a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) characteristics and motor control using Typhoon HIL software for both real-time simulation and testbench control. A PMSM with 5 pole pairs has been chosen for this endeavor. The complete system has been modeled using Typhoon HIL. In the simulation environment the PMSM, the three-phase inverter with the sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) and the control were implemented. For the physical testing of the motor, Typhoon HIL 604 platform has been used. As for the software, not much has been changed to control the real testbench. The same control method has been applied to the testbench and the inverter. For the latter an internal modulator was replaced with a simple 3 phase modulator that is sending the control signals to the physical inverter.

articleTitle: Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm for Optimal Installation of DSTATCOM into Distribution System based on Various Voltage Stability Indices
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this article is proposed a new approach based on an Arithmetic optimization Algorithm (AOA) that can notably envisage with diverse problems for optimal installation (locate and size) of Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM) in Electrical Distribution System (EDS). An approach applied for optimal installation of DSTATCOM units in EDS is used as the new multi-objective functions to minimize the Active Power Loss (APL) and various voltage stability indices. The voltage stability indices applied are the Voltage Stability Index (VSI), the Fast Voltage Stability Index (FVSI), the Line Stability Factor (LPQ), and the Power-Voltage Stability Index (PVSI). The methodology is tested on IEEE 33-, and 69-bus EDSs. The results of the simulation confirm that the optimal installation of DSTATCOM plays a significant role in EDS, where excellently reduced the power losses and enhanced the voltage profiles.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of Sensorless Control for PMSM Based on Neuro-fuzzy Speed Controller
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Starting from the capabilities of controllers developed using the fuzzy logic on modeling and equalization of nonlinearities, just as the mathematical model of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) is nonlinear, this article presents a control system of a PMSM based on three neuro-fuzzy controllers ensuring the continuous adjustment of the tuning parameters Kp and Ki of the PI-type speed controller. When there is a high-dynamics PMSM rotor speed reference and a significant variation of the load torque, using a PI controller with fixed tuning parameters, even when using a Particle Swarm optimization (PSO) technique will result in inferior results as opposed to the case when the tuning parameters are adaptive. Thus, an observer of the rotor speed and of the load torque is additionally presented in the case of the sensorless control. The first two neuro-fuzzy controllers prove their superiority due to the high-dynamics speed reference, and if there are also significant variations of the load torque, a third neuro-fuzzy controller is required for additional adjustments in order to achieve superior control performances. The validation of the proposed control system is performed by numerical simulations in the Matlab/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Long-term Energy Analysis of a Wastewater Treatment Plant with Biogas Production-Case Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The energy consumption of a high-capacity wastewater treatment plant (up to 900,000 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> wastewater/month), equipped with biogas production and energy recovery installations, was analyzed via long-term monitoring (76 months). The recorded data during the monitoring period show that the total active electricity (EE) consumption of 8,130,324 MWh (at an average power factor of 83.81<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> treated wastewater, where the share of consumption related to biological aerobic and anaerobic processing stages is predominant (62.17%).

articleTitle: Energy Consumption in Wastewater Treatment Plants
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In 2020, the energy consumption and volumes of treated wastewater in four village wastewater treatment plants WTP (with a capacity below 10,000 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/month), were monitored monthly. The acquired data showed that the specific energy consumption at the investigated WTP (depending on the period and location) was between 1.561 and 2.580 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> treated wastewater, the annual averages being between 1.786 and 2.334 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (depending on WTP). Moreover, the consumption given by the equipment related to the biological treatment lines BgT primarily determines the total energy consumption in the WTP-the average annual values of the BgT share in the total energy consumption of the investigated WTP were between 0.632 and 0.729. These findings conclude that the WTP energy efficiency improvement is possible primarily by streamlining aerobic and anaerobic biological treatments.

articleTitle: Power Quality Evaluation in Autonomous Wastewater Treatment Plant
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The power quality of a low-capacity domestic wastewater treatment plant with autonomous operation through automatic control of the technological process was analyzed by monitoring/recording the main electrical parameters. Determinations showed that, under concrete operating conditions (average effluent flow 9.8 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/h, 5.9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C water temperature in aerobic and anaerobic bioreactors), the average active power absorbed is 11.103 kW at an average power factor of 0.73- which leads to a specific consumption of 1.125 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> treated water. The evolution of the active power, reactive power, apparent power, power factor, total harmonic distortion of the voltage (THD V), and total harmonic distortion of the current (THD A) parameters show fluctuations determined by the consumers' operating sequences. The frequent starts/stops of inductive consumers by electromagnetic contactors produce transients reflected on the evolution diagrams of the power factor and THD (both in voltage and current).

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling Assessment of Electromagnetic Interference Between Power Lines and Metallic Pipelines: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The rapid change in human migration from rural areas towards the biggest metropolitan areas across the world implies a reorganization of the utility transport networks creating new common right-of-ways between high voltage power lines (HVPL) and metallic pipelines. In this paper, induced voltages from HVPL to metallic pipelines are calculated using different numerical approaches. The induced voltages along a metallic pipeline are computed using the wide-known circuit theory and electromagnetic field theory approaches embedded under ATP, EMTP-RV and XGSLab software packages, respectively. In order to accurately quantify the impact of different topologies on the induced voltages along the pipeline, the length of the parallel routing, as well as the separation distance, are varied during the computational domain. Moreover, the CIGRE WG 36.02 criteria regarding the equivalent parallel sections are applied when circuit theory is employed and verified using the adopted electromagnetic field method.

articleTitle: Real Time Broadband Electromagnetic Spectrum Monitoring System based on Software Defined Radio Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation and testing of a broadband real-time electromagnetic field monitoring system. The system is based on a Software Defined Radio (SDR) platform that allows the implementation of three synchronous reception channels. The tests have been performed both in laboratory conditions and in case of measuring signals emitted by a wireless device connected to the 4G communication network. The results of testing showed that the system has real-time monitoring capabilities for a channel with a bandwidth of at least 10MHz.

articleTitle: IoT power monitoring device using Wi-fi and Arduino
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Reliable real-time power measurement data represents a vital role in understanding energy behavior from a consumer standpoint. Energy efficiency is directly influenced by monitoring electric parameters. With collected live data, the challenge becomes how to organize and analyze datasets of information. The purpose is to design and build a low-cost electronic monitoring device using Arduino and IoT for electricity monitoring. The main capabilities are to measure, record, and transmit using wi-fi connection all the essential electric parameters in a web-based application. Monitored electric parameters are voltage, current, power factor, phase angle, power, and energy. The developed prototype is versatile in multiple types of low voltage installations, mainly household appliances. Measurements are transmitted remotely in an online database, where the data can be stored and analyzed in real-time. The solution has permanent storage and facilitates consultation of past and current records. The market approach is possible because of the low-cost of the device. A commercial version would be suitable and could easily integrate Smart Grid applications. Using real-time energy data and monitoring software, consumers can measure high consumption loads, reduce base loads, evaluate peak and off-peak hours and identify irregularities. optimize usage scheduling and track energy-saving targets and goals more accurately.

articleTitle: Methods of Faults Detection and Location in Electrical Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main goal of the present paper is to bring a personal and an objective view over the particularities for methods of fault detection and location in electrical systems. The paper is structured in four sections. The introduction section highlights the importance of detecting and locating the faulty elements in an electrical power system. Types of faults are described in the second section of the paper. Section three focus over the methods of detecting and locating faults in an electrical system analyzing in detail each of these methods: time domain reflectometry, impedance based method, traveling wave method and knowledge based method. The last part of the paper emphasizes from an objective point of view based on details offered by the previous section the characteristics of each method described.

articleTitle: Allocation of Distributed Generators Using Parallel Grey Wolf optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper solves the allocation problem of distributed generators (DGs) in smart grids utilizing a grey wolf optimization (GWO) algorithm. By parallelizing GWO, it presents the impact of using various number of processors on speedup, efficiency. To decrease the computation time required to perform the simulations, different migration rates are applied for different number of processors. Moreover, the accuracy obtained using different number of processors is analyzed. The simulations are performed for a 33-bus distribution test system using MATLAB's parallel computing toolbox. From the simulation results it is observed that parallel GWO can be used as a tool for distribution system optimization.

articleTitle: A Romanian Solution for Real-time Monitoring of Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Based on the need to make more intensive use of transmission system infrastructure, transmission system operators (TSOs) have begun to investigate what are the most appropriate measures to achieve this goal. For TSO, the construction of new transmission lines is not a simple procedure, mainly due to strict environmental regulations. It is becoming increasingly clear that replacing, building and equipping with the necessary new lines will become one of the important problems difficult to achieve, which can jeopardize the achievement of the EU's 20-20-20 objectives. Therefore, a new approach has become mandatory in order to increase the efficiency of existing electricity networks in a safe way and to deliver the required energy in a timely and economical manner.In Romania, the technical conditions for the on-line OHL monitoring systems are mentioned in the internal technical norm “Technical specification for complex system for online monitoring of overhead power lines of CNTEE Transelectrica SA”. The monitoring system is appropriate to be used for 110 kV, 220 kV and 400 kV overhead lines.The paper presents the OHLM system, a Romanian innovative system for online monitoring of the operational parameters of the OHL's (based mainly on real-time measurements, such as: current through the line, conductor temperature, conductor inclination angle/sag, mechanical tension of the line, conductor oscillations, etc.), that includes also intelligent electronic devices for acquisition / processing / storage and remote data transmission (to the power system operation dispatcher / the power system diagnosis and condition monitoring center / the data management center, etc.).

articleTitle: An Improved Metaheuristic Algorithm for Load Balancing in LV Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Energy efficiency is a major concern for utilities. For electricity transmission and distribution companies, while efficiency can be achieved by replacing old equipment from the networks with newer devices, or incorporating into the existing infrastructure additional components, these measures should be applied only after all other options, which do not incur additional costs, are exhausted. The paper proposes a metaheuristic approach to solve the phase load balancing problem in low voltage (LV) electricity distribution networks (EDN) that uses a hybrid Differential Evolutionary Particle Swarm Optimization (DEEPSO) algorithm for single-phase consumer allocation on the three phase of the LV network, used for optimal phase load balancing. The results obtained for a real LV distribution feeder from a urban area using the information provided by smart meters demonstrate the performance of proposed approach, with comparison to the classic PSO.

articleTitle: Virtual labs – challenges, opportunities and practical lessons learned
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This article discusses challenges and opportunities for virtualizing laboratory exercises in university courses in order to allow for remote teaching. Besides addressing the design of such virtual laboratories in general, it also highlights the impact of urgent needs for course re-structuring resulting from the Corona pandemic. Two case studies for entry-level and major courses in Power Engineering are presented.

articleTitle: Romanian innovative system for power losses real time monitoring and analysis in electrical transmission and distribution systems
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In the process of power supply to final consumers, an important amount of energy is lost in the transmission and distribution systems due to technological and non-technological losses. Technical losses represent an economic loss with environmental effects at national level, and its optimization should be performed from an overall national's perspective, regardless of the institutional organization of the sector and ownership of operating electricity utilities. The volume of energy losses in the power transmission and distribution systems is important, as it is generally up to 3 - 13%. The volume of power losses in Romanian power transmission and distribution systems is important, the level being of about double to the average in Europe. The current paper presents the research results of the authors regarding the real time monitoring and analysis systems for power losses, in electrical transmission and distribution systems.Within the research project, it was developed a dedicated system, successfully tested within a 5 years partnership with CNTEE “Transelectrica” - SA, on a transformer of 250/250/80MVA 400/121/20 kV from 400/110 kV Pelicanu Substation and respectively on the 400 kV overhead power line (118 km) Bucuresti Sud - Pelicanu.The tests results showed the importance of evaluation by real-time measurements, compared to the results of evaluations by calculations, of active power losses at power transformers and overhead power lines, respectively. Values several times higher were found for the values of active power losses measured online, in real time, than those determined by calculations.Online measurements have shown that there may be cases when large industrial consumers produce current and voltage harmonics well above the maximum allowable limits specified in the standards. The harmonics are transmitted practically undamped by the windings of the power transformers and on the transmission power lines (in the case of tests, even more than 100 km away from the place of their production).The online measurement of active power losses on the 400 kV overhead power line, 119 km, showed that corona losses are insignificant especially during periods of atmospheric humidity below 85%, and that active losses on power lines are practically resistive losses. The resistive losses on the measured high voltage overhead power lines are much higher than the calculated ones. The difference is determined by the fact that the calculation of active power losses on power lines includes the value of ohmic resistances of conductors evaluated based on line conductor resistivity or possibly based on ohmic resistance measured at a certain moment, and not the real value of the ohmic resistance of the line in real time (which changes over time due to the change in the state of the multitude of joints of the OHL conductor sections).

Author Keywords: Power Losses online measurement and monitoring

articleTitle: The Risk Analisys for the Coexistence of Overhead Lines and Urban Green Areas
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The key challenge of smart cities is the need to satisfy the conditions for a safe distance between the buildings, streets, or green areas (public gardens) and the classical high voltage overhead line. If the interference effects are high enough, they may pose a safety hazard to personnel or the public or may compromise their integrity. This paper is the result of the authors expertize that determines how close to high voltage power lines, public gardens can be used. The coexistence study is a technical-economical documentation in which both mechanical and/or electrical assumptions of the overhead lines are delimited based on inspections, calculations, measurements, etc. The location of other capacities or networks on the elements of the corridor or its protection and, where fitting, the obligation expected to satisfy the conditions of coexistence granted for by the rules and the costs of such operations. This research has been limited to generally available materials. Finally, to highlight the impact and risk analysis provided by the coexistence between the high voltage power line and urban public gardens a real study case is presented.

articleTitle: Numerical Modelling and Analysis of Circular Patch Antenna Array for Further Use Determination
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Microstrip antennas are made on ceramic substrates or dielectrics, for example polystyrene, quartz or sapphire. In comparation to the other types of antennas, microstrip antennas have reduced dimensions, thus they are easy to integrate. The radiating patch can have a lot of shapes such as square, circular, rectangular, dipole, elliptical. This paper represents a study about the different parameters of the circular patch antenna arrays and the influence of the feeding and positioning on their functionality. The S parameter, directivity, specific absorption rate and efficiency are analyzed for 3 structures, considering also the influence of the dielectric material used.

articleTitle: Analysis of Walking Cell PWM Strategy in Multilevel Frequency Converter in Fault Condition
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Cascaded multilevel frequency converter contains low-voltage cells in each leg. Bypassing the failed cells ensures the uninterruptable operation of a frequency converter. However, it can lead to a unbalance phase-to-phase voltages. A special control algorithm is required to operate under faulty conditions. Most approaches based on the phase-shift pulse-width modulation and level-shift pulse-width modulation are considered in this paper. However, these techniques have limitations, such as time delayed operation which limits current loop response time when reference voltage changes and in case of the cell failure. This paper proposes a modulation strategy which solves these problems. It implements pulse-width modulation in a single cell with sequential cell switching and can rapidly adapt to the failure of any cell without impact to the quality of the output voltage. The operation of the proposed pulse-width technique under faulty conditions was verified using Simulink Model.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimal Renewable Distributed Generator Integration in Distribution Systems Using Grasshopper optimization Algorithm Considering Overcurrent Relay Indices
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The endless problem of energy supplies is always floating on the surface. As a result, there is a daily improvement to optimize power generators and power system configuration. Renewable Distributed Generators (RDGs) are at the heart of these developments. The optimal placement and sizing of RDG sources is a recent problem in the Distribution Power System (DPS) that is usually solved using various algorithms due to its high complexity. A new optimization algorithm called Grasshopper optimization Algorithm (GOA) has been implemented to optimize different types of RDG units for obtaining an optimum allocation of multiple Photovoltaic Distributed Generator (PVDG) and Wind Turbine Distributed Generator (WTDG) units in DPS. This paper proposed new Multi-Objective Functions (MOF) that are considered to minimize simultaneous the total of Active Power Loss Index (APLI), the Voltage Deviation Index (VDI), the Operation Time Index (OTI), and enhance the Coordination Time Interval Index (CTII) of the primary and backup overcurrent protection relays installed in DPS. The proposed algorithm is tested on a standard IEEE 33-bus distribution power system. The numerical simulation including comparative studies was presented to demonstrate the performance of the GOA and compared to that of the Particle Swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm, and Sine Cosine Algorithm (SCA).

articleTitle: Exponential Smoothing Model for Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The aim of the paper is to develop a method for short-term deterministic and probabilistic photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting, and to present the results for an actual applicative case study. The proposed method is based on the exponential smoothing models, and two variants of this approach are analyzed within both the deterministic and the probabilistic frameworks. In particular, the probabilistic forecasting method is developed through an ensemble-based procedure that includes point forecasts obtained through several smoothing exponents. The case study discussed in this paper is based on experimental data obtained from an existing plant, and the corresponding results are compared with a benchmark based on the persistence model. It is found that the proposed exponential smoothing method significantly improves the result of the short-term PV power forecasting, both in the deterministic and probabilistic frameworks.

articleTitle: Trajectory planning of a 3-RRRRR planar parallel robot
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to determine the optimal trajectory planning algorithm of the moving platform of a planar 3RRR parallel robot between two points according to imposed velocity profiles to achieve smooth movement among the imposed trajectories. Two velocity profiles were studied: constant speed profile and trapezoidal profile. These profiles were determined analytically and implemented using MATLAB together with the equations that solve the inverse kinematics problem (IKP) to determine the required behavior of the generalized coordinates complying to the velocity profiles over an imposed trajectory. The movement of the robot was simulated using MATLAB library, Simulink SIMSCAPE and Dassault Systems SolidWorks to impose the same velocity profiles over the trajectory and compare the results with the results from MATLAB.

articleTitle: Protection of power systems by earthquake warning based on local assessment of seismic events
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In order to limit the material damages and the human victims caused by some earthquakes, a complex system of protection of high-risk equipment and installations were designed, built and tested in Râmnicu Vâlcea (Romania). Such are the power supply systems and electrical networks that have a warning in case of major earthquakes based on the local measurement / assessment of seismic events. The system was validated by the comparative presentation of the data recorded on the occasion of two recent seismic events -the earthquake of Mw = 6.4 of 2020/12/29 with depth = 10 km Croatia and the earthquake of ML = 4.2R of 2021/02/27 with depth = 125.9 km, Vrancea. The latter was felt in the area of Râmnicu Vâlcea at a distance from the epicenter of 633.9 km and 173.09 km, respectively, producing vibrations with an acceleration of 0.52 mm / s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 0.28 mm / s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> respectively. These values were below the 1.2 mm / s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> threshold (considered dangerous for gas and electricity networks) and no warning and command signal was issued.

articleTitle: Arduino Platform for Optimized Irrigation in Strawberries Fields
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper is focused on the development and implementation of an autonomous and automatic system for irrigating in a strawberry field. For this purpose a smart irrigation system using Arduino was created. The software takes into account information related to water tank level, soil moisture and solenoid valve position, while providing farmers with daily information about the state of the culture. The output values of the sensors transmitted to the microcontroller are analyzed and, depending on the threshold imposed by the user, a decision is made whether to water the plants or not. Thus the microcontroller gives the command to open or close the solenoid valves. The water level in the tank used to supply the installation is also monitored using an ultrasonic sensor. System information such as date and time, soil moisture in the three areas, the condition of each solenoid valve and the amount of water in the tank are displayed in real time. The results yielded by different tests confirmed the functionality of the irrigation system, which remained in operation throughout the season.

articleTitle: Complete liberalization of the energy market a challenge for the household consumer
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In order to comply with the provisions of Regulation (EU) 2019/943 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 June 2019 on the internal market in electricity, the Romanian Energy Regulatory Authority (ANRE) has ruled that starting with January 1, 2021 the market of electricity is completely liberalized, the supply of electricity will be made in a competitive manner. The regulation stipulates that the prices are formed according to supply and demand and Romania thus complies with this provision. Domestic consumers, but even commercial and public ones, found themselves in a position to analyze the offers received from competitive suppliers given that the overwhelming majority knows nothing about the liberalization process, the components of the contract price, what are the conditions of supply on who can negotiate them etc. This article aims to make an up-to-date x-ray of the Romanian energy retail market and to be a useful tool for the home consumer in choosing the competitive offer that best suits him. Due to the reaction of the media and associations representing the interests of household customers, especially the Intelligent Energy Association, the ANRE Order 5/20.01.2021 extended the transition period until 30.06.2021 and some measures were taken to simplify the transition from universal service to the competitive market.

articleTitle: PM-assisted Synchronous Reluctance machines for light electric vehicle propulsion system-comparative analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The battery voltage in Electric or hybrid vehicles is switching from the classic 24 or 48V batteries to ones using 400V or higher. In this paper, two electric machines supplied with a 560V DC-link will be designed and optimized using a classic design approach and using a 120V DC-link supplied electric machine as reference. As the market for rare earth magnets is in decline, the proposed machine type is a Synchronous Reluctance Machine (SynRM) assisted with Ferrite magnets placed in the flux barriers. A comparison is performed between the two machine variants using the FEA method, in order to validate the performances of the machines.

articleTitle: Students’ Perception on Integrating Collaborative Tools into Electrical Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The interest in teaching methods for Electrical Engineering (EE) education has been particularly depicted within Virtual Learning Environments. Applying a quality assessment and comparing the results with adjacent engineering fields may provide meaningful feedback on transferable teaching-learning skills. We adopt the perspective of the usability criteria as a quality assessment dimension that could augment a Technology Acceptance model and we investigate the integration of collaborative and productivity tools to support educational processes in EE VLEs. The case study has been conducted among the EE undergraduate students in the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Romania and results have been compared to the adjacent engineering profile of Electronics, Telecommunications and Information Technology, consolidating the applicability of such a model for VLEs.

articleTitle: Identifying the Conditions of Maximum Electricity Demand Coverage in a Direct Mode, by Wind and Photovoltaic sources
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: To reach the objectives of energy security and updated NDC targets, 100% RES scenario is considered for the R. Moldova. The specific goal of this study is to identify the conditions under which a maximum coverage of the annual electricity demand can be obtained directly from WF+PV sources. Two approaches are used to reach the goal: WF and PV cover energy demand in a direct mode without considering the balancing power - Technical Weight, and second, WF and PV cover the demand in a direct mode together with a source of balancing power - Gas turbine (GT) - Economic Weight. The results obtained: When the capacities of WF and PV are determined in a way to produce electricity equal to annual power demand, Technical Weight is equal to a maximum of 71-72%. If WF and PV electricity produced is higher than demand by 50%, WF+PV tandem may cover the energy demand in a direct mode at maximum level of 80.5%. Five variants of WF, PV and GT economic parameters variation were considered when these sources are operating together. The calculations done and analysis performed showed that: The minimum price of electricity produced by WF+PV+GT in V1 (basic variant, current data) takes place at a PV integration level of 18% (Zopt). At WF specific investment of $750/kW (V2), compared to $1445/kW in V1, Zopt is equal to zero. That is, at such WF specific investment, PV implementation is not feasible. Price for electricity is lower than in V1 by 25.4%. Even at a specific investment of about $1000/kW for WF, the minimum energy price is obtained in the absence of PV. Decreasing PV specific investment by up to 50% (V3) compared to the level established in V1 has little influence on the maximum Technical Weight. The electricity price is lower than in V1 by circa 8%. A 25% decline in TG specific investments (V4), or a 17% drop in the price for natural gas (V5) compared to V1, have no material effect on the maximum Technical Weight.

articleTitle: Extracting the Operating Characteristics of Hydropower Plants Using a Clustering-based Efficient Methodology
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: To benefit from all advantages of a hydropower plant, seen as a renewable source, reliable and low cost of the injected electricity in the power grids, the Hydro Plant Operator (HPO) must ensure the optimal operating regimes and an efficient maintenance program. In this context, a clustering- based methodology has been proposed in the paper to determine the representative operating characteristics (ROCs) of a hydropower plant, considering time slices associated with each generating unit. The results have confirmed the performance of the proposed approach from the point of view of the computational time and the quality of partition obtained associated with the patterns of the operating characteristics. These patterns can represent the support offered to the HPO to provide for an optimal operating of a hydropower plant.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of Auxiliary Power Supply Systems for a Nuclear Power Plant (NPP)
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Reliability has a considerable role in Nuclear Power Plant safety and availability. A Nuclear Power Plant needs to be able to produce power in safety condition and economic efficiency. The Auxiliary Power Supply System is an important point in architecture of a Nuclear Power Plant because among of economic role, the system has a much more important role, namely to keep the reactor core in safety condition under various operating regimes of Nuclear Power Plant. The objective of this paper is to use a quantitative and qualitative technique in order to perform a reliability assessment of Auxiliary Power Supply Systems for a Nuclear Power Plant.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Electrode-Pipeline System for Reducing the Corrosion Process
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The corrosion process for underground pipes is a particularly important aspect for those who deal with the distribution of gases or other products. The need for an anticorrosion cathodic protection installation proves to be essential for prolonging the service life of the pipes. One of the possible solutions is a system for injecting a current into an electrode placed near it. This paper analyzed different situations of placing the electrode next to the pipeline and also different constructive shape of the electrode. Numerical analysis is performed by considering various soils where the pipe can corrode (clay, slit, sand), varying the conductivity of the environment. The results revealed the innumerous parameters that are to be considered for a proper quantitative investigation of this phenomena.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of Grid-Connected Photovoltaic System Based on Fractional-Order PI Controller and Particle Swarm optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Starting from a benchmark implemented in the Matlab/Simulink development environment for PV array connection to the grid, this article compares the performance of the DC circuit voltage control system using the Proportional Integral (PI) controller, the PI-Particle Swarm optimization (PSO) controller, and the Fractional-Order (FO)-PI-PSO controller. The article presents the topology and the mathematical description for a connection between a PV array and the main grid. Besides are presented the main elements which assure the connection: the temperature and solar radiation simulation block, which represents the input for the PV array block, supplying DC voltage to the DC-DC (Boost converter block), the DC intermediate circuit, the DC-AC converter receiving DC voltage at the input, the filtering block, and the transformer for the connection to the main grid. The superior performances are obtained through using of the differential and integral fractional calculus and the optimization of the PI/FO-PI controller parameter tuning using the PSO method. The validation of the superiority of FOPI-PSO voltage controller over a benchmark system is carrie out by numerical simulations by using Matlab/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Temperature Influence on Electrical Conductivity of PVC-TiO2 Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The role of the TiO2 nanoparticles on the frequency dependent electrical conductivity of PVC and on its variation with temperature is discussed in this paper. Thus, the DC and AC conductivities of PVC-TiO2 nanocomposites and unfilled PVC are analyzed from dielectric spectra of the real part of the complex conductivity and imaginary part of the complex relative permittivity, over a frequency range of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> -10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> Hz, and for temperatures from 310 to 340 K. The results obtained show significant lower conductivity values in PVC-TiO2 nanocomposites with respect to those for PVC, and consequently a significant improvement of electrical insulation performances in nanocomposite as compared to the unfilled PVC, for all the tested temperatures. The increase of the temperature leads to higher DC conductivity in both unfilled PVC and nanocomposite, showing that the electrical conduction is a thermally activated process in these materials. The activation energies for the thermally activated DC conduction in PVC-TiO2 nanocomposites and in PVC were obtained from Arrhenius plots.

articleTitle: Using JTAG to debug Modern Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to dispel some of the myths around what JATG is and about what JTAG isn't, in order to facilitate one's understanding of the overall debug process for TMS320C2000 and other microcontrollers used in various control systems relevant to power and control and how to use JTAG to debug the complex modern power systems of today.

articleTitle: Chip structure metallization impact on thermally induced faults in power IC devices
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: IC's power devices are widely used in many applications like switched-mode power supplies, power drivers for mechanical actuators, etc., being subjected to repetitive power pulses. The Active Power Cycling (APC) influences the reliability of IC's, hence the failure rate. The failure mechanisms observed in MOSFETs power devices based on contacting clip technology [3] are solder fatigue and metallization layer degradation. The difference between the Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) of different materials can induce high deformations in chip metallization, like wrinkles at the top power metal layers. It is well known that the temperature swing is responsible for the IC's degradation, but many other parameters e.g. geometrical dimensions, material properties etc., have an important impact too. This paper studies the impact of geometrical dimensions on thermal-induced stress and deformations by a contact clip on a typical MOSFET metalization structure.

articleTitle: Direct-Current Motor Speed Control Using a PID Discrete Controller
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The presented paper aims at designing a PID discrete type controller, obtained using Kalman Method, to control the speed of a Direct-Current Motor. Such a DC motor is used as the actuator for the driving mechanisms that load or unload billets from a rotary hearth furnace, to yield seamless tube pipes through hot rolling. For each supplying machine, from or towards the furnace, a direct-current motor supplied through a direct-current converter is being used. The mathematical model of this actuator is obtained as a second order transfer function, starting from the system of equations that describe its working in transitory regime. To obtain the PID discrete control law that can be easily implemented on a microcontroller, few steps must be performed. First the continuous mathematical model is converted into a pulse transfer function, and further on, the steps from Kalman designing method are applied. The initial controller is a higher order controller that generates good transient regime specification, for the step response of the controlled structure (meaning the motor's speed), however the control signal variation is not feasible, due to high negative values. Adjustments are applied, by substituting the real negative pole, yielding a PID discrete controller. The resulted control signal generates a feasible range and the discrete control law is much simpler, thus being easier to implement to ensure the imposed speed of the motors and to assure the machines correct positioning. The results assessment is made via simulation, using MATLAB computer software.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of double-axis orientating Low Concentration Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The output of a photovoltaic module can be increased through different techniques, and the concentration of solar radiation is one of them. Consequently, a low concentration system was designed considering the double-axis orientating modules of the photovoltaic power plant of the ENERED's research platform within the “Gheorghe Asachi” Technical University of Iasi, Romania. The performances of the obtained LCPV system were analyzed in terms of power output, operating temperature, and efficiency losses due to the increase of operating temperature.

articleTitle: Three-winding Transformers Design by means of Differential Evolution Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The aim of the paper is the development of an optimal design for the sizing of a three windings transformer. The sizing was carried out through the solution of an optimization problem so that the leakage reactances are available within a fixed range to reduce the couplings between the two secondary windings. The optimization problem was solved with a software that uses finite element method to improve settlement procedure based on a differential evolution algorithm. Starting from an initial population of transformers, through the differential evolution we obtained the optimal solution which fits perfectly the required specifications.

articleTitle: Overmodulation Operation of Two-Level PWM Inverters of Photovoltaic System with Double-Delta Configuration of Winding of Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents results of investigation of operation (in the overmodulation control zone) of two three-phase inverters of photovoltaic installation with double-delta-sourced winding of power transformer. It has been shown, that schemes and algorithms of synchronous multi-zone pulsewidth modulation (PWM), developed and modified for synchronous adjustment of inverters of photovoltaic system in the zone of overmodulation, insure synchronization, symmetry, and improved spectral composition of both output voltage of inverters and the corresponding winding voltages of multi-winding power transformer.

articleTitle: Functional Characteristics of a Multichannel Frequency Converter
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper is dedicated to the study of methods related to improvement of functional/operating characteristics of a frequency converter with circular voltage phase rotation. In order to improve frequency conversion quality, the use of multichannel switching circuits is proposed. To implement the multichannel principle, matching transformers have been developed, as well as control laws for the proposed devices. The study results show the effectiveness of the proposed method for improving the characteristics of the frequency converter and the possibility of using these type devices for organizing controlled intersystem connections on alternative current to combine power systems operating with different frequency standards.

articleTitle: Low-cost environmental monitoring system for incubators used in maternity hospitals
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper proposes a low-cost solution for an incubator that can be used for premature newborns, intended to monitor and control external and internal parameters of temperature and humidity. The work involves interfacing the sensors and the Arduino system to LabVIEW and the actual design of the incubator. The monitored parameters will then be processed and stored in a file dedicated to each newborn.

Author Keywords: monitoring and control of two different parameters (internal and external temperature and humidity)

articleTitle: Regulation of Voltage and Reactive Power in AC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The research is aimed at developing effective solutions for creating Microgrid and integrating them with external power systems. One of the important technological tasks in this case is the regulation of the voltage when the Microgrid is synchronized with the external power system and the parallel voltage operation mode is implemented with the difference in the levels of the desired voltages in the Microgrid network and the external power network. To solve the problem, it is proposed to use innovative patented devices- normalizers of alternating voltage NORMEL™ on Microgrid connections with the external electrical network. The paper presents the results of the analysis of the conditions and possibilities of voltage and reactive power regulation, modeling Microgrid modes exclusively of alternating current, both in terms of generation and the electrical network, including synchronous connections with the external power system. The results are based on the experience of creating such Microgrids based on cogeneration power plants with the capacity of up to 25 MW with gas reciprocating.

articleTitle: Optimization of electricity power losses using Smart Metering systems in Romania
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Smart metering systems are electronic systems that measure the electricity consumption, ensuring a secure two-way transmission of information to the end customer and providing more information than a conventional meter, using electronic communication. This type of smart metering technologies has been implemented in three pilot projects from a Romanian region, in order to ensure the collection, analysis and processing of electricity specific data, as well as the connection/disconnection of each consumer. The implementation of smart meters in the three pilot areas led to a more accurate recording of final electricity consumption and a detailed monitoring of the electricity consumption by types of consumption profiles, as well as the electricity technical power losses (ETL) indicator. This paper aims to analyze the evolution of electricity technical losses registered by smart metering systems in each of the three pilot projects and also for the whole region in a certain period, in order to demonstrate the need and importance of monitoring this type of power losses and to find the best methods to reduce them, using smart metering. The results showed that the cost of electricity for the technical power losses in the chosen area is very high. In order to reduce these costs, a number of measures for ETL optimization and reduction were proposed.

articleTitle: Romanian TSO’s Augmented Reality Concept
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper aims to present Transelectrica's concept of augmented reality, based on a series of technical specifications adapted to the digitization requirements of the Company and highlighting the benefits of implementing this technology. Through this study, there will be identified the work processes within the operation and maintenance activities that are subject to the risk of human errors due to the lack of clear and effective training, or the assistance of an expert. The proposed solution is to implement the concept of augmented reality on equipments installed in transmission substations. A demo version will be presented, which can then be replicated in other pilot projects of the Company.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Full Bridge Modular Multilevel Converter for High Voltage DC Transmission Using Various Pulse Width Modulation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The modular multilevel converter with full bridge submodules is becoming one of the most attractive topologies for high voltage DC transmission, since it enables fault handling at a converter level, thus reducing cost associated to DC circuit breaker. This is especially useful in scenarios where fault conditions are more prevalent, specifically in applications that rely on overhead transmission lines. This paper performs a literature review regarding existing pulse width modulation techniques that are applicable for full-bridge submodules and provides a comparison of converter performance for all analyzed methods.

articleTitle: Study of Parameters Influencing the Electrical Locomotives Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper is focused on an intensive study relative to the analysis of efficiency-related indices characterizing 2 electrical locomotives working in tandem to tract freight trains. Software was conceived to process many data acquired from the train (absorbed and regenerated active and reactive energies, geographical coordinates of the route, speed, meteorological conditions etc). In order to reduce the influence of declivity over the final results, data were acquired for both senses of running over the same route. Statistic data related to other identical locomotives for 12 consecutive months were used to derive conclusions related to the influence of meteorological conditions all over the year. The average results obtained from the 3 analyzed round trips selected in some of the efficiency-related worst scenarios from the environmental conditions point of view matched the average results computed across a whole month for a set of 10 locomotives and allowed to draw useful conclusions.

articleTitle: Proof of concept system for supporting energy efficiency in office buildings
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: A green certified office building will allow for a high occupancy level and market value, while reducing with up to 30% the operational costs. The certification looks at energy efficiency, use of renewable energy, a healthy indoor environment, etc., requiring focusing on sustainable measures and solutions starting with the concept phase. Our paper aims to increase the level of Building Automation Systems (BAS) in green buildings by supporting the planners and constructors with an overview of the main standards currently in place and by introducing a new proof of concept system for monitoring the ambient parameters. These ambient parameters are mandatory in upper layer control systems that increase wellbeing while reducing energy consumption.

articleTitle: Improving the vibration reliability testing process
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Automobiles are a necessity in every aspect of our life, regardless the use of it: personal, transportation of people, transportation of goods, agriculture, constructions, etc. When we purchase an automobile, we consider aspects of design, performance, scope of use, etc. In order to have the guaranty that these parameters are met, they need to be tested and validated by the producer. Validation is a stage in which the validity of a product is proven. This stage is part of the reliability testing process, a necessary process to ensure the quality of the manufactured components. During a lifetime of use, the components must withstand numerous disturbing or damaging factors. Some of these factors have a mechanical origin and can affect the functionality of the component. Some of these mechanical factors are vibrations that can be divided into 2 categories: periodic vibrations (sinusoidal vibrations) and nonperiodic vibrations (random vibrations) and mechanical shocks of different shapes (half-sine, initial/terminal peak, triangular, rectangular, etc.).

articleTitle: A Method Based on Amplitude Probability Density Representation for Sounding High Frequency Noise in Ionospheric Channels
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: High Frequency (HF) communications efficiency require a precise characterization of the ionospheric channel’s noise. We present a rapid and accurate method to sound the HF ionospheric channels that enables tracing of the time-availability of the channel based on imposed electric field strength thresholds. The method makes use of the amplitude probability density implemented in a real-time spectrum analyzer. Sounding of 3, 10 and 20 kHz bandwidth channels in the 4.8 – 8.8 MHz range is exemplified and specific observations are presented.

articleTitle: Studying the impact of Dynamic Line Rating on the Romanian Power Transmission Grid
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper aims to study the impact of the implementation of Dynamic Line Rating (DLR) on an extended number of overhead lines from the Romanian Power Transmission Grid. Dynamic Line Rating comes handy for the current trend of widespread adoption of renewable energy into the main transmission grid, which may be subject to severe variability. DLR may prove to be the gaining technology, when large capacities are needed to transit the transmission grid, for covering the renewables' inadequacy.

articleTitle: Interlaboratory Comparison of Electromagnetic Fields in Power Supply Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This interlaboratory comparison is performed for two reasons: to ensure the repeatability of testing amongst EMC laboratories concerning specific test methods and to evaluate the testing capabilities of these laboratories. The purpose of this paper is to present the application of an interlaboratory comparison method for electromagnetic fields produced by power supply systems, involving two laboratories. An electromagnetic field generator with a frequency of 50 Hz, which is moved from one laboratory to another, is used in order to obtain the data for the final assessment. The results obtained were based on the three-point measurement method in accordance with the standard IEC 61786.

articleTitle: Wind Power in Romania Energy Mix Towards Sustainable Development
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to highlight the current status of wind energy in Romania renewable energy mix, in the context of fulfilling the goal 7 for 2030. Wind energy is an important renewable source in Romania, highly available, reliable and sustainable. In the last decade, there was an increased interest in developing new wind facilities, in order to reduce the energy generated by non-renewable sources, such as coal, gas or oil. In this paper were assessed, based on energy reports and the climate action simulators, perspectives on renewable energy development.

articleTitle: Tissue thickness and pressure measurement solutions in life-saving surgical procedures
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper attempts to demonstrate the need of implementing measurement solutions to surgical mechanical staplers. The object of the writing is to present a working electronic system that can be implemented in a circular surgical stapler and to bring solid conclusions after testing on animal tissue. The setup contains an Arduino-based system together with a required sensor, placed on an already existing surgical circular stapler. Measurements and results are described with the goal of defining the range of appropriate compression that can be exercised on the living tissue, without leading to side (negative) effects.

articleTitle: Planar Spiral Inductors Parameter Extraction needed to design a Wireless Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The wireless power systems of millimetre dimensions are nowadays used for a wide range of high technology applications. In this paper we aim to extract the planar spiral inductors parameters to optimal design them for the design of a wireless power supply system used to supply the peacemaker or other similar devices. The planar spiral inductors are analysed first to extract their specific parameter. Then the influence of the ferrite on the spiral inductors parameters is analysed to improve the inductor performances by increase its inductance. Next using the optimized inductor, a wireless power supply system is designed and 3D numerical modelled to also extract its parameters. Different distances between emitter and receiver inductors are considered trying to estimate the real possible distance that can exist between them if they will form the wireless power supply of a peacemaker. Finally, we analyse the influence of ferrite, considering different thicknesses, also on the wireless system's parameters, aiming to increase them for improvement of device performances.

articleTitle: Geographical distribution of renewable energy production for maximum efficiency and environmental sustainability
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In the last decade, the world has experienced a rise in the usage of renewable energy, and this is done with the need to ensure that there are environmental conservation and optimal efficiency in the usage of the available energy. The desire to ensure that the world becomes reliant on green energy has led to the development of the programs that support subsidiary regimes. Renewable energy sources are not depleted, and different parts of the world have various resources that they can use to generate renewable energy. The climate change issue has led to the environmental bodies in the world, advocating for the various states to adopt measures that will ensure that they manage to meet the rising demand for energy while remaining environmentally sensitive. The calls have led to the adoption of programs causing increased investment in the renewable energy sector. The environmental conservation groups are essential to the realization of these goals. In this paper four case studies consisting of Kenya, China, Bangladesh and the United Kingdom have been illustrated which address the impacts and uses of renewable energy for electricity generation. Geographical variables for the installation of energy plants have been highlighted as the prime purpose of their distribution across countries in order to attain environmental sustainability as well as optimum hazard-preventing energy production. This will allow us to take informed decision in installing the power plants in accordance with the resources to achieve green energy.

articleTitle: Optimization of The Control Circuit of A Wireless Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Traditional wireless power transfer systems typically adopt the single-frequency control method to ensure a constant output voltage and current for different applications. This paper presents a different side of the control circuit of a wireless energy transfer system, i.e. input is made with two frequencies aiming to optimize the wireless energy transfer.The purpose of this paper is to show how it can be increased the efficiency of a wireless power system, in comparison with the traditional wireless power transfer systems with a single command frequency. An experimental prototype will be buit in order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed wireless energy transfer system and the control method.

articleTitle: Aspects Regarding the Presence of TCSC Devices on the Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Reactive power limit of power system is one of the major causes of voltage instability. Power system can be adapted to improve voltage stability by adding reactive power sources such as capacitors, synchronous compensator, or Flexible AC Transmission System (FACTS) devices at the appropriate locations. One of these devices is TCSC (Thyristor Controlled Series Compensator). This device is used to control the reactance of the transmission line on which it is installed. This paper will present in which way the power network is affected by the presence of TCSC device.

articleTitle: Edge data processing using Kalman filter
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The evolution of the modern power grid is closely tied to the advances in the telecommunications field. Data transmission from the field no longer poses a problem, but the large volume of data generated that needs to be handled, continues to be a challenge. As a direct result of the continuous push for digital technology integrations within the power grid, Electric Utilities have gained extended capabilities with the help of SCADA (Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition) system and its various applications used for control and visualization of real-time data received from the process. SCADA systems help human operators to make informed decisions and integrates various devices in order to achieve Smart Grid capabilities by using a Distributed Control System architecture to control geographically dispersed assets. Smart Grids utilize a series on services and products in order to promote the penetration of renewable resources, together with control, monitoring and self-healing technologies. This paper aims to explore the role that Edge plays in the flow of data, starting from the place where data is generated until it reaches the Cloud.

articleTitle: A Simple and Low-Cost Equipment for Derating the Power Distribution Transformers Subjected to Distorted Operating Currents
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper suggests a simple and affordable device that allows the fast and continuous in-situ calculation of operating parameters of the in-service distribution transformers that supply nonlinear loads. The proposed equipment is a system with an architecture based on two interconnected modules, mainly realized of electronic boards. The first one monitors and acquires the current power quality parameters at low-voltage part of the investigated transformer along with the ambient temperature. The second module performs the data processing, analysis, and results visualization. The computing algorithms for the transformer derating parameters consider the international recommendations. They are implemented in the developed device by using a dynamic programming language allowing a proper programming of the electronic boards. Accordingly, the equipment manages to preserve the transformer well-operating parameters, maintaining the continuity of energy supplied to nonlinear consumers. Supplementary, the device has low costs, is very flexible (suitable for transformers with rated power up to 2000 kVA) and can be easily adapted for remote data transmission.

articleTitle: Implementation of technology in physical activities designed for students
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Physical education has a very important role in the development process of the young generation but also in the preservation of the population's health condition. To achieve these benefits, one of the most important aspects regarding physical education classes is the constant concern of PE teachers for developing the students necessary skills and abilities for the independent practice of various forms of physical activity throughout their lives and increasing the number of hours allocated to sports. For students, everything that has to do with technology, (smart-phones, smart-watches etc.) has become a must have. This also applies in the sport area. While using technology, people can monitor their heart rate, number of steps, pace, distance and have a real feedback on their physical activities. Also, using technology has made it much safer, fairer, and more attractive to practice sport. The technological improvements will continuously have a big impact on sports.

articleTitle: Demand side response in the electricity market
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Demand response can be defined as tariffs imposed on electricity based on the usage changes by end-users for a specific period. Additionally, it refers to a way of reflecting the benefits of efficiencies in production or the management of power companies. It can either be price based or incentive-based. Examples of prices-based responses include Real-Time Pricing (RTP), Critical Peak Pricing (CPP), and time of use (TOU) tariffs. An analysis of the role of electricity companies on their customers' consumption behavior by exploring the cases of Bangladesh, Kenya, UK, and China has shown that there is a need to ensure that the understanding of electricity rates in the global population is changed. The different strategies adopted by electricity companies of the countries considered are all aimed at influencing consumer behavior to reduce the stress on the electricity grid. The relationship between the price and the supply of electricity in response to consumer demand is presented in this paper. The production, management and supply of electricity by power companies has been extensively addressed, taking into account four different countries, such as Bangladesh, China, Kenya and the UK. It provides an overview of how demand side responses have been addressed on the premise of different time spans and consumption according to consumer behavior.

articleTitle: Forecasting Methods to Support the Decision Framework of Prosumers in Deregulated Markets
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In the present paper, a profit maximization problem for a prosumer is formulated and solved. The prosumer selects the electricity procurement approach among the pool market and forward contracts. Instead of treating the system marginal price as a stochastic variable, a price forecasting method is employed to forecast future prices. The prosumer owns a generation photovoltaic (PV) unit and sells the produced electricity into the network. To estimate future revenues, a PV power forecasting is proposed. Also, in order to estimate future bill savings, a load forecasting method is utilized for the prosumer's daily load curves. The forecasting procedures for all three variables allows the prosumer to act strategically in the competitive electricity market and maximize the profitability. A comparison of forecasting algorithms is held in order to examine the influence of the forecasting accuracy in the profit maximization objective.

articleTitle: Contributions to Monitoring the Condition and the Protection of Insulated Bushings, Pertaining to Transformer Units
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In order to comply with the need for safe and quality electricity transmission, it is necessary to provide an adequate operating condition for the main electric power pieces of equipment. The capacitor-type bushings pertaining to the transformer units are such important components, which must retain their parameters throughout their operating life. The paper presents the design of a system for monitoring the condition of insulated bushings pertaining to transformer units: the presentation of the hardware, of the software and the practical implementation. For the study and analysis of solutions, as well as the development of the application, six insulated bushings of a 400 kV autotransformer were considered: three insulated bushings of 200 kV and three of 400kV.

articleTitle: The Impact of Distributed Heat Pumps on the District Heating System
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The Republic of Moldova have presented, in March 2020, to the Secretariat of the UNFCCC the second Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC2). The country’s new economy-wide unconditional target is to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 70% below its 1990 level in 2030. The economy-wide conditional target, in NDC2 is up to 88% below 1990 level, if a global agreement addressing important topics including low-cost financial resources, technology transfer, and technical cooperation, accessible to all, is secured. The implementation of the NDC2 targets will require major change in current model of energy use in the country, in particular the advanced heat pumps are one option for district heating systems to secure clean and affordable heating for the people. The paper presents results of TIMES modeling of district heating system scenarios to year 2050, with consideration of climate change targets of NDC2. The results show that with CO2 emissions limits, the gas fired CHPs are replaced by distributed heat pumps at the consumers side. The results were obtained in the framework of the of the State Program 20.80009.7007.18: “Eco-innovative technical solutions for improving energy consumption in buildings and the smart grids development options with advanced integration of renewable energy in Moldova (SYNERGY)”.

articleTitle: Smart assessment methodology in physical education classes
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Smart Sports Industry is a very promising area which has a big potential for an effective assessment of the students. By using technology, the human errors can be reduced, and the evaluation of the students is therefore an objective one. SMART is used to describe the five simple criteria that are followed when setting a certain goal: specific, measurable, attainable, relevant, and timely. The critical concept for teaching students is setting a goal. This is a fundamental skill that must be settled so that the evaluation is successful. The smart concept must be associated with smart devices that can monitor the motion. That is why using technology in sports can be a revolutionary area that could and will be developed more and more in the next period.

articleTitle: The Simulation of Li-Ion Batteries Using Series-Parallel Cells in Different Modes of Operation
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper is focused on simulating the discharge of Li-Ion batteries using series and parallel cells in different modes of operation. The simulations are realized using Matlab/Simulink. Two cases are analyzed for the system under test: constant discharge current and a variable discharge current. In these cases the batteries were considered 100% or partially charged. For a series cell we used four batteries and for the parallel connection we used three series cells. The simulated waveforms for the state of charge (SoC) and the output voltage of batteries are presented for the analyzed cases.

articleTitle: The Influence of Feedwater Preheaters on the Power Plant Thermal Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: According to the new statistical reports of world energy, coal-fired energy production still stands over 30% of total energy production worldwide. It is already demonstrated that the use of regenerative preheating leads an increase in the thermal power plant efficiency as a whole. The present paper focuses on the optimal number of regenerative preheaters used and on their location: on the low pressure side or on the high pressure side. The study was conducted on a 300 MW thermal power station equipped with an intermediate super heater, the initial steam parameters at the turbine entrance being: 170 bar pressure and 540°C temperature. Finally, the increase or decrease of the thermal efficiency for each analyzed case is illustrated. The most favorable case and the most unfavorable case are highlighted.

articleTitle: Method for Designing a Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper presents a method used for designing a photovoltaic system, this using a program called the program “Calculator sizing photovoltaic system”. Depending on the electricity consumption obtained from the bill (on grid system) or based on the consumers used in the household (off grid system), the necessary solar panels are obtained, not before choosing the power range of the panel. Within the program there is a list of powers range, for solar panels ranging between 125 W and 480 W, being the most common on the market. It also includes suggestions for components such as solar panels, on grid or off grid solar inverter, bidirectional meter, solar charge controller, batteries, solar tracker, accessories, or off grid or on grid photovoltaic systems, which users can apply to determine the amount invested. Depending on the amount invested, the amortization period can be determined, but, for on grid photovoltaic systems, the amounts collected for the number of MWh delivered in the network are not taken into account, nor for the green certificates obtained according to the number of MWh injected into the national grid. Currently, for a delivered MWh, the amount of 39.90 €, according to the national course BNR, is received from the electricity supplier, a price that is regulated by the order of the National Energy Regulatory Authority (ANRE) or for each MWh injected into the grid, two green certificates are granted, worth € 25 each.

Author Keywords: computer program used for photovoltaic system design

articleTitle: Fuzzy logic controller for regulating the indoor temperature
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In recent times, globalization and energy efficiency policies have further required temperature control applications in different daily activities, especially with the greenhouse effect. In residential buildings, water and living space heating consumes most of the primary energy. The paper presents a method to keeping the comfort temperature in living space by using an approach based on an artificial intelligence technique, namely fuzzy logic. The support for the proposed method is an electrical hot-water radiator heating system with a tankless heater. The fuzzy logic controller makes a continuous regulation of the indoor temperature by adapting the temperature of the heating agent regarding the indoor and exterior temperature. To validate and test the proposed method, MATLAB-Simulink was employed. The comparison with an On/Off controller that is the most used control device due to financial benefits showed the efficiency of the fuzzy logic controller.

articleTitle: A comparative analysis of model-based control methods applied for the active suspension system
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Scientific research and technological advances in recent years on car suspensions have led to an increase in their dynamic performance, improved passenger comfort and safety.
