The importance of the field is also given by the need for continuous increase of traffic safety factors in the context of infrastructure development and implicitly the increase of driving speed. The paper presents the classification of suspensions and methods used for modelling, simulation, and control of active vehicle suspensions. The Matlab environment was used for simulation and control design. Several control methods and comparisons between them are presented and implemented by simulation. A consistent part of the paper presents an MPC type control method applied for the control of the active suspension. Possible future developments are highlighted.

articleTitle: Analysis of kinematic dexterity based on a 2 DOF incompletely restrained cable-driven parallel robot
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The study is based on a 2 DOF incompletely restrained cable-driven parallel robot whose number of cables is equal to the degrees of freedom of the robot. The main goal of this study is to analyze the kinematic dexterity of the robot according to the available workspace defined by the tensions in the cable, which need to be between a minimal tension to prevent the cable from sagging and a maximal tension to prevent the cable ripping under an imposed handled mass and the own mass of the cables. The dexterity of the mechanism is used for expressing the movement ability of the mechanism among a specified direction inside the total workspace. The condition number of the Jacobian matrix is used for evaluating the dexterity of the mechanism. The study presented above was implemented using MATLAB to solve the equations that compute the local dexterity indices of each point inside the workspace and for implementing a graphical representation of the results.

articleTitle: Study of lightning’s strokes on HV overhead power lines
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main objective of the current study is to analyze how the high voltage overhead power lines behave on lightning direct strokes. Once the lightning strike hits the active conductors, towers and ground wires the transient regimes appear, which are analyzed in the present paper with ATP simulations. Also, using some ATP-models, the insulators flashovers are simulated, using their voltage-time characteristics. These results are being presented, as well as a comparison between them and the basic mathematical model.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Radiation Generated by Dielectric Barrier Discharge
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The present paper assesses the electromagnetic fields near the dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma reactor, for different distances and for two distinct cases: shielded and unshielded power supply during plasma generation. The plasma electrical discharge is generated in atmospheric conditions (pressure and humidity) by an AC high voltage power supply between two circular plane-parallel metallic electrodes. The plasma is applied for treating the surface of polymeric films, increasing thus their hydrophilicity without destroying the inner properties of foils. The interferences are induced by electrical surface discharges for which there were measured both vertically and horizontally radiated fields, in order to ensure personal and electrical appliances safety.

articleTitle: Responsiveness of a web application and debugging of the API
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Testing the performance of an application is required to deliver a program free of bugs and errors. It is required to do customization on the procedure we must follow to control and evaluate how specific part of the system will perform. Sometimes the usage of a single software is not enough because it is necessary to do a thorough full test of the whole application. When the system under testing is a web based one then the availability of the service and the handling of thousands of requests which might be done in the shortest time possible is a must for such systems. There are many tools that you can be employed to do the testing but between them there are two very efficient and accurate one.

articleTitle: FPGA implementation of fixed-point arithmetic voltage mode controller for the Buck converter
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: A digital implementation of the voltage mode control for buck converters was designed and demonstrated on an FPGA development board. The digital control uses a fixed-point structure that increases the control accuracy without increasing the number of arithmetic operations. A soft-start function was included to minimize the output voltage overshoot at startup; an over-current protection function was also integrated in the experimental setup. The buck converter was designed to supply 3. 3V from an input voltage ranging from SV to 16V. Measurements results presented in the paper validate the design: 61mV maximum overshoot on startup; load transients of 164mV overshoot and 145. 5mV undershoot for a load jump from 150mA to 1. 1A, line transient of 236mV overshoot and 21SmV undershoot for 4V line jump and 44mV maximum output voltage ripple. The control loop stability margins were also assessed through measurements: they shown a minimum phase margin of 38.5° and a minimum gain margin of 11dB for a 16V input voltage and a 1. S4A load current.

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy Consumption in Public Buildings
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper proposes to analyze the actual energetic consumption in a typical building and to verify the energy quantity that may be achieved by applying energy efficiency actions. To obtain energy optimization in public buildings we chose the building of the “Energetic'' High School in Cluj-Napoca. It is a building that comprises ground floor and three floors built before 1970. It has 16 rooms on each floor. After an energy audit we identified the sources of electrical energy, electrical circuits, main consumers. We analyzed hourly curves of energy consumption. Based on the consumption data we identified the impact of energy efficiency measures, replacing the equipment to reduce the energy consumption and the Greenhouse Gas emission and improving the interior comfort We proposed introducing high energy efficiency technologies, modern systems of measurement and control, energy management systems for continuous monitoring and evaluation of energy efficiency and forecasting the energy consumption. An important contribution of our paper consists in simulations in Matlab that allow the correct evaluation of the energy consumption for the analyzed situations.

articleTitle: Smart Grid Lab Hessen – a real-life test environment for active distribution grids
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper describes the setup of the laboratory used in project “Smart Grid LAB Hessen” in order to study the interaction of OT and IT systems from different manufacturers within low-voltage (LV) distribution grids. Starting from a literature review on small-scale LV benchmark systems, a general small-scale grid topology for smart LV distribution systems is derived. The topology is flexible enough to model both rural and urban distribution feeders.Also taking into account the limitations from the available laboratory equipment by applying suitable scaling factors

articleTitle: The Influence of the Geometric Shapes of the Component Elements of the Planar Filter on its Parameters
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Today, in the age of 4G and 5G technologies, the continuous development of high-tech devices through their minimization and various forms of design for their components that need to comply with EMC standards, make the analysis and design of EMI filters to be a research topic of great interest that will certainly stay that way for many more years. In this context, the present paper proposes the analysis of the influence of the geometric shapes of the elements that compose a planar EMI filter on its parameters. On one hand, we will follow the self-parameters of the component elements, and on the other hand, the minimization of the parasitic parameters will be followed. The analyzes will be performed on a low pass filter, which is the main element of the filter for the suppression of the electromagnetic interferences.

articleTitle: Comparative study of CAD optimization features for the workspace of 3DOF Parallel Robot
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In today's industrial use, one of the most implemented parallel manipulator is the Delta robot. In this paper we analyze the inscribed workspace of the prismatic actuated 3 DOF Delta parallel robot from a geometric perspective by determining the analytical relationship between the lengths of the arms, the radius between the prismatic axes, the total stroke of the prismatic joints and the volume that describes the whole workspace. Determining the relationship mentioned above, allows us to implement an optimization algorithm to determine the configuration that generates the workspace with the largest volume, representing the largest workspace achievable considering the limits imposed preceding the optimization process.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis through Block Diagram for a Hybrid Lighting System
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper represents an analysis of reliability indicators through the concept of the block diagram (RBD). The analyzed device is an intelligent lighting system based on a hybrid electricity system. It is a multifunctional autonomous device designed for street lighting, being at the same time a powerful platform for urban monitoring, internet access and mobile telecommunications.Since new directions of development of the energy sector are pursued, the reason for choosing this device is that it represents an autonomous system that uses renewable sources by operating in parallel two systems (wind system and photovoltaic system) of energy conversion that allows increased safety in power supply and achieving superior efficiencies.This hybrid system is an intelligent lighting system fully powered by solar and wind energy. Its unique design combines advanced aerodynamics with simple geometry and allows continuous functioning in urban areas. The photovoltaic cells cover the upper surface of the casing as the turbine directs the wind flow to a diffuser, thus creating an accelerated effect in the energy store in the battery, which serves as a platform for additional services.Reliability Block Diagram is based on a visual representation of the relationships between the system relative to its components. RBD represents the model of a system based on the operation rate, respectively defect rate of the components.

articleTitle: Analytic synthesis of a four-bar mechanism as part of a reclining mechanism
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The method presented in this paper is based on the synthesis of the four-bar mechanism considering two or three imposed positions for the coupler link of the mechanism and its length and determining the required lengths of the other links and the positions of the fixed revolute joint in order to achieve the prescribed position. This method represents an analytical approach of the geometrical method used for the mechanism synthesis. A numerical example was developed, and the geometrical synthesis problem was studied using Dassault System Solidworks and compared with analytical method that was computed using MathWorks MATLAB. The obtained mechanism represents a part of a complex structure representing a reclining mechanism for an armchair, for which desired positions of the seat, backrest and footrest are imposed.

articleTitle: Low Cost Foot Pressure Measuring Device
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper aims to present a system that can accurately measure the flat pressure using mainly the force applied during various movements of a body. To create an accurate measuring device, we have studied the possibility to put a supplementary sensor-base between the foot and the shoe. We have begun studying human mobility after seeing that the modern systems used the diagnostic feet healthiness are discovering more affection worldwide. This type of device is accurate and offers a variety of results for standing, walking, climbing stairs, or even working out if the suggested limit is not passed. The major problem pointed was the client usage because points must be calculated and remapped for both feet of any user. This procedure makes possible either the flat pressure measurements or even the basis of a system used to harness kinetic energy and store it for various mobility purposes.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Small Power Zero-Airgap Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the behavior of a small power zero-airgap induction motor. The structure is in fact an induction motor with eccentric rotor that touches the stator in its rotation movement, so that the local airgap is zero. The utility of this kind of motor is given by the fact that in some application an eccentric movement is required and, in this way the mechanical part can be removed leading to a higher efficiency of the whole system and a compact system. Based on a previous study that provided the optimum variant of a small power induction motor from the point of view of number of poles and rotor bars we analyze here by numerical means the influences of the eccentricity on the performances of the machine. A comparison between the skewed and non-skewed rotor bars induction motor is presented in the paper. Few conclusions regarding the possibility to use such a motor for a considered application are brought in the final part of the paper.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of two magnetic bearings topologies
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Current industries that use high-speed rotation systems are starting to replace the standard mechanical bearing systems with magnetic suspension systems. This tendency to replace mechanical bearings is due to the advantages of magnetic bearings, for instance low losses, high reliability lubrication free operation and the ability to work in vacuum Magnetic bearings can allow the suspension of a rotor without any mechanical contact in rotating machinery which can produce a high rotating speed and position precision, thus removing the problems introduced by mechanical bearings such as low dynamic stability, thermal lock, and limited rotation speed This paper deals with design procedures for two different topologies of active magnetic bearings (AMBs) that might be applied for a high-speed machinery. The virtual prototypes of the magnetic bearings are created and simulated, and a comparative analysis of magnetic bearings is performed.

articleTitle: Speed and Rotor Flux Estimation using Back-EMF MRAS and Gopinath Observers for Sensorless Vector Control Systems of Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents a new technique of implementing the back-EMF MRAS speed observer used in sensorless vector control systems with induction motors. The adjustable model of the speed observer is made on the basis of the estimated d-q components of the back electromotive forces (Back-EMF) using in this sense the afferent components the space vector of the rotor flux, obtained on the basis of the reduced order Gopinath observer. The testing and evaluation of the dynamic performances of the speed and rotor flux observers are by numerical simulation in Matlab-Simulink performed.

articleTitle: Open source software based design and optimization tool for electrical machines
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents an open source software-based design and optimization tool for Switched Reluctance Machines, which uses Python language and FEMM software. The validation of the tool will be performed in this study and the main goal for future is to extend the possibilities to design other types of electrical machines such as the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM) or Synchronous Reluctance Machine (Syndrome).

articleTitle: Transient of High Voltage Circuit Breakers Intelligent Switching during Grid Faults
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The transients in power system may be induced by the switching of high voltage circuit breakers, thus affecting the power quality. Intelligent switching is a form of controlled commutation coordinating the instant operation of a circuit breaker with a custom point on an electric parameter waveform. In this paper was assessed the possibility to reduce the aperiodic component of the short-circuit current using intelligent switching. The paper highlights the controlled switching using circuit breakers and power electronics. The simulation model was built in EMTP software.

articleTitle: Smooth Control of Shed ACLs Capacity based on the Minimum Conversion Time Matching
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the shed capacity provided by the aggregated air conditioner loads (ACLs) fluctuates greatly and difficult to be effectively utilized. This paper proposes a minimum conversion time matching (MCTM) model to realize the smooth output of the shed capacity. Proceeding in two steps: First, grouping the ACLs by working power. Get the switch conversion time to minimize the shed capacity fluctuation by coordinating all ACLs switch simultaneously. Second, determine the switch state to minimize the ACLs switching frequency and the shed capacity fluctuation in the next cycle according to the single cycle closing potential of every ACL in the switch moment. By these two steps circulation, give full play to the ACLs scheduling capacity. The simulation validates that the proposed model can output the shed capacity smoothly with different ambient temperature and setting temperature range compared with the temperature dead band approach (TDB).

articleTitle: Integration of Air to Water Heat Pump into District Heating System with Combined Heat Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: the scope of the work is solving the multicriteria task - determination of the optimal ratio between the heat rejected from the return water and the external air for designing of heat pump of maximum efficiency. The goal has been achieved by resolving the following tasks: energy efficency calculus of Combined Heat Power Plant (CHPP) with district heating pumps using a part of return water heat and using ambient air as source of low temperature heat for hot water production, elaboration thermodynamical cycles for heat pump.

articleTitle: Deicing system for high voltage overhead power
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Providing electricity transmission and distribution services is a complex process, of major importance and with implications in all areas of activity. Therefore, the provision of these services at the highest possible level must be a constant concern of all specialists in the field. This paper aims to address an issue of great importance for high voltage networks and with a significant impact in ensuring the stability of the energy system.

articleTitle: Integrated approach in designing photovoltaic power plant
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In the context of a continuous increase of energy demand that contributes to the acceleration of climate change, at a global level special attention is paid to energy efficiency activities. In the beginning, this paper evaluates the energy sector at global, European and national level, therefore, an overview of the evolution of renewable energy sources over the last few years is elaborated, focusing in particular on the current situation and development prospects of the photovoltaic sector. The main objective of the authors is the design of a photovoltaic (PV) park located in Romania. Using PVsyst software, the optimal sizing and configuration of the system was performed, as well as an estimation of the future performances of the installed equipment. To determine the economic and financial effects of the implementation of a photovoltaic park, three different scenarios on the payback period of the initial investment and calculation of some financial indicators was performed.

articleTitle: Advanced Control Design for Anti-Lock Braking Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The anti-lock braking system (ABS) is the core of a vehicle's active safety system. It basically ensures the vehicle's steering, preventing the wheel lockup in any braking conditions and shortens the breaking distance. The dynamics of the ABS system are highly nonlinear which makes the control problematic. The proposed solution tries to overcome the nonlinear dynamics and characteristic uncertainties by taking them into account in the controller design stage. The effectiveness of the proposed solution is tested at first on a nonlinear mathematical quarter car model in Matlab/Simulink environment and then on a laboratory setup offering good braking results, improving the active safety the vehicle under heavy braking conditions.

articleTitle: Shape optimization for the inscribed workspace of a prismatic actuated 2PRR parallel robot
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to analyze a set of geometric shapes inscribed in the workspace of a prismatic actuated 2PRR parallel robot by optimizing either the geometric parameters of the inscribed shape to maximize the total area achievable or the parameters of the robot to achieve the best fit for the imposed shape. The goal presented above is implemented analytically by using the equations that describe the whole shape of the workspace and determining the equations of the imposed shape by determining the intersection or the tangency points of the imposed shape with the whole shape of the workspace. The equations that define the shape inscribed in the workspace are used in the optimization process by determining the parameter configuration that maximizes the area. Furthermore, the optimization process was implemented with Dassault Systems Solidworks library, Design Study, and the results were compared with the analytical solution.

articleTitle: A Comparative Assessment of Magnetic Concrete versus Ferrite for a High Power Inductive Coupler
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The air pollution in large urban agglomerations can be drastically reduced by electrical mobility which covers all means of road transport: personal cars, freight cars and especially buses. All of them are dependent on the existence of charging stations that are able to ensure the charging of their batteries at home, in parking lots, on the route or in depots. Compared to the classic, conductive charging (Plug-In), contactless charging (Wireless Power Transfer - WPT) is a disruptive technique with numerous advantages that allows static, semi-dynamic (opportunity charging) and dynamic charging (on route) of batteries. This paper refers to the WPT transfer via an inductive magnetic coupler that is embedded in the pavement and must withstand heavy car traffic without damage. This paper also assesses the possibility of replacing the brittle ferrites used in classical constructions with Magnetic Concrete (MC). It presents the choice of concrete mixture composition, the experimental determination of its magnetic properties and an analysis on the electromagnetic efficiency of the WPT system for different magnetic coupler structures, through Finite Element (FE) simulations.

articleTitle: Impact of Demand Side Management on the Self-Sufficiency and Self-Consumption of Buildings with Photovoltaic and Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Integration of Photovoltaics (PV) with Energy Storage Systems (ESS) and Demand Side Management (DSM) is an innovative way that could transform a building into a self-sufficient nanogrid. Such an approach could act as an energy rehabilitation solution and contribute to alleviating the technical problems posed to the electrical grid from high consumption of buildings and high PV injections. The scope of this paper is to investigate the potential for achieving high level of building self-sufficiency using hybrid PV-ESS-DSM solutions. Towards this direction this work analyzes the self-consumption and self-sufficiency rates for various installations equipped with PV and ESS with different climatic and load demand characteristics. Moreover, the potential for increasing these indices under DSM is examined aiming to maximize the utilization of renewable energy produced on-site.

articleTitle: Optimal location of a PV system using Grey Wolf Optimizer and operation analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: With the rapid integration of renewable energy technologies and the development of smart grids in the last decades, the role played by the electric power distribution system is increasingly important in power systems. The photovoltaic industry knows a significant growth due to the political commitment that helps to achieve environmental goals and the security of energy supply in order to create a future sustainable economy. This paper presents a methodology for determining the optimal location of a photovoltaic (PV) system in a distribution network using Grey Wolf optimizer (GWO) algorithm. The objective function consists of minimizing the active power losses. The results provided by the GWO are compared, in terms of performance with those obtained by a genetic algorithm (GA). Furthermore, an operation analysis is performed on an hourly basis for a one-year period. The influence of connecting the PV system upon the active power losses, voltage magnitude and lines loading is also analyzed.

articleTitle: Energy Pulse – the Efficient Solution for Monitoring Electricity Consumption from Decentralized Data Sets
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The present work brings to the reader's attention the benefits and facilities of the Energy Pulse application. The application enwraps a complete solution for real-time monitoring of electrical energy consumption of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, the Swimming Pool Complex from Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, the Faculty of Building Services, and from Mărăşti Student Campus. The use of a new algorithm for dynamic allocation of threshold parameters for the detection of outliers together with the development of a new algorithm for generating average consumption led to more accurate results by 42.421% and faster by 99.625% than the results generated by classical methods.

articleTitle: Smart Hub Electric Energy Data Aggregation Platform for Prosumers Grid Integration
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Clean energy generation is the aim of the actual energy strategies for a climate neutral society and economy by 2050 in EU. The renewable energy distributed generation} (DERs) has reshaped the face of modern power systems, forcing them to adopt smart grid specific functions. The actual major challenge is to improve the market access of small commercial and residential customers and to exploit their flexibility capabilities by implementing Demand Side Management (DSM) actions. Also, the increasing number of prosumers, connected to the grid, will help to increase grid capacity for green energy generation if the new challenge to implement proper actions for energy generation side management of prosumers will be addressed. Smart metering and sub-metering IoT devices provide smart homes/hubs with the operational data and control abilities needed to perform such actions, while new and disruptive technologies, like blockchain, enable peer-to-peer transactions and contribute to the required tamper-proof character of energy transaction data. One major challenge of small commercial and residential prosumers is not only to exploit their flexibility capabilities by implementing Demand Side Management (DSM) actions and VPP specific functions but also to improve their market access. A feasible scenario involves the creation of aggregators, mainly for the management of smart homes demand response (DR) actions, and smart energy hubs for flexibility management actions of prosumers. The paper describes the Smart Hub Electric Energy Data Aggregation Platform (SHEEDAP.2) presenting its structure, functions, and performances. Some possible applications in Romanian economy are also indicated.

articleTitle: The impact of Power transformers on the Energy Performance Indicators of the power distribution grids of industrial end-users transitioning towards environmental sustainability
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: As the European Union adopted the Green Deal [1] and proposed the framework for achieving climate neutrality by the end of 2050 [2], industrial end-users are more focused than ever on achieving the highest possible environmental impact reduction. The main focus of future investment in the industrial sector will now be on diminishing the CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2, eq</sub> emissions, in order to maintain financial stability, especially in the context of the fourth phase of the EU-ETS mechanism [3], which implies a constant reduction in the number of CO2 certificates allocation until 2030. This will lead to a potential decrease of investment in the electricity end-use efficiency of various industrial sectors. In this paper, the economic impact generated by the power transformers in various industrial end-users boundaries, relative to actual operating scenarios was analysed in order to determine the best course of action for the sector to minimize the operating costs with the internal power distribution grids.

articleTitle: A review of residential micro–Combined Heat and Power systems based on renewable energy
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the last micro- Combined Heat and Power technologies developed for residential buildings. The focus in on two types of technologies, internal combustion engines and fuel cells. The aim is to present technologies concerning different types of primary renewable energy, auxiliary equipment, size of thermal storage size, electrical and thermal energy produced, CO2 emissions and least cost operating strategy. The paper is expected to be helpful as a literature review presenting many combined heat and power technologies for micro cogeneration, trigeneration or multigeneration along with efficiency and the benefits, most of them using renewable energy as primary. The revised technologies include those with Stirling Engines, Solid oxide Fuel Cell, Proton Exchange Fuel Cell Membranes adapted or integrated with many components and varieties of combinations to obtain the highest possible efficiency and exergy. Therefore, they can be used depending on the heat demand or the energy demand.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Romanian pilot site energy consumption indicators and technical prerequisites in the implementation of the RE-COGNITION Horizon project
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main ambition of the RE-COGNITION Horizon 2020 project (https://re-cognition-project.eu/), in which Technical University of Cluj-Napoca is involved, is to develop a future and technology-proof integration solution aiming to maximize the utilization of the energy that is locally produced by building-level Renewable Energy Sources (RES) technologies, and the reduction of implicit and explicitly induced costs. In the frame of the project, a RES Integration Platform is developed, which incorporate existing, as well as newly developed RES and storage components, along with peripheral electrical and thermal load equipment (HVACs, chillers, ICT devices, conventional load equipment etc.). The RES Integration Platform aims to optimize the building energy flows, regardless of type and conditions. Several pilots with different building environments and climate zones, all around Europe, will be selected to test the RE-COGNITION framework components. This will sufficiently fulfil the validation purposes of the developed technologies and comply with the end-user needs. In this paper, we present the general description of the Romanian pilot site, as well as the energy consumption indicators measured in the last 3 years prior to the project's start. An analysis of the local context which provides the technical/socio/economic constraints that the project should handle is also presented.

articleTitle: On Beneficial Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) Services
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: A number of studies have investigated the possibility of extending Electric Vehicle (EV) Lithium-ion battery life by deliberately choosing to store the battery at a low to moderate state of charge. Recently, there has been considerable interest shown in the scheme of a deliberate discharge and subsequent recharge of a battery to yield an overall reduction in battery degradation whilst carrying out Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) services (so-called `beneficial V2G'). This paper presents an investigation of the conditions permitting successful operation of this method by examining incremental time variation of the relevant parameters for two types of cells from results of the same physical size and chemistry, and similar capacity. These two types of cells are found in this present analysis to offer differing degrees of suitability for beneficial V2G.

articleTitle: Aspects of Data Models compatibility within Substation hybrid LANs
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present various communication protocol conversions aspects and Data Models Mapping compatibility among different communications standards used in a power substation network. At one side is IEC61850 and on the other side are legacy protocols such Modbus RTU, IEC 60870-5-103, IEC 60870-5-101, and its extension IEC 60870-5-104 to suit the complete network access. The Data Models Mapping are translated, either by the bay controller or the substation main communication Server, from a hierarchical and tri-dimensional model of IEC 61850 to a linear-plane data models of legacy protocols, and vice versa.

articleTitle: Small-Scale Substation Model-From Design to Implementation
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper explains a micro-controller board’s adaptation to emulate a substation utilized to control power system equipment. The goal was the utilization for teaching electrical engineering technology students. This working model demonstrates and teaches students how power systems are wired and controlled using protective relays. The first part describes the overall substation board wiring diagram, how the electronics were selected, what the board looked like after construction, and provided a cost estimation of the whole project. The most common electronic device selected is an Arduino Mega micro-controller. All the substations control depends on the controller’s operation abilities. The next topic covered the types of protective relays and power system control options that the board features. The three specific relays the board can implement are 50, 51, and 59 protective relays. It also explains how all these features work and other concepts are programmed into the board to mitigate improper control, such as inrush current. The results and data gathered to prove that the board’s design, construction, and programming methods are very closely the industry-standard control practices addressing power systems. The findings verify that the main objective of creating a working small-scale substation model was a success.

articleTitle: New Approach using Optimization Method in Forecasting of the Own Technical Consumption in Distribution Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Nowadays operation of the power distribution networks is constrained by the currently active regulations but also by some other factors that are conditioned by its beneficiaries impact or by economical restrictions. In this work the second category of factors is tackled by identifying and forecasting in an optimal approach one of the most important terms in indirect control of the energy contour which is impacted by the own technical consumption.Own technical consumption in distribution grids is one of the most relevant performance indices related to the efficiency operation and sustainable development of power grids. For this reasons, it is considered as an essential monitoring parameter in regulatory and supervising governmental agencies in energy domain. At this level of importance the power distribution operators are willing to determine and to estimate the evolution of this parameter for their internal needs as a factor in decision making and for reporting to the regulatory organizations. The paper's main goal is focused on development and analysis of this performance index forecasting. Two approaches are evaluated, namely the data series based linear regression model estimation and a novel multi-criteria optimization forecast method.In order to validate the proposed approaches, a case study is performed and the outcome results and analysis are presented. The proposed methodology and how the most relevant obtained results can be deployed and implemented by the industry are illustrated.

articleTitle: A novel concept for designing the energy efficiency program
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The European Green Deal reveals a new approach related to energy systems sustainability, assuming climate neutrality by 2050 for EU achieved only under a sustainable economy, meaning decoupling economic growth from resources use under social equity conditions. This paper presents a novel approach for designing an energy efficiency program, converting it to the sustainability's energy-use investment program. The concept proposes a life cycle assessment methodology for evaluation of energy efficiency solutions (LCAMEPEES), gathering several innovative elements which have not been used at once so far in energy performance evaluation. First, the methodology sets the purpose of energy performance assessment to the level of sustainability evaluation. The LCAMEPEES introduces for the first time a complex multi-criteria analysis model, addressing four evaluation criteria with complex key performance indicators (KPIs). The tool allows to appreciate the contribution of each energy-use system to the main priorities of Green Deal: use of sustainable technologies (scored under technical criteria) to ensure climate neutrality (ecological criteria) through a transformation of society and Europe's economy under cost effective (financial criteria), fair and socially balanced conditions (social criteria). The methodology proposed in this paper is a useful working tool in energy efficiency investment planning. Using in the design and planning phase of an energy project of a preset list of measures types, as guidance for synthesis of all possible actions to improve system's performance, requires a thorough analysis of investments needed towards converting to a sustainable system. Another novelty brought by LCA-MEPEES refers to the list of key indicators proposed for performance evaluation, providing, in addition to current practices, information about overall performance, energy flexibility, ability to respond to occupant needs and profitability. Using such KPIs, an energy use systems will be able to generate information for optimization operation scenarios while get prepared for their integration into smart grids. For the evaluation objectivity and accuracy, LCA-MEPEES proposed key performance indicators synthesized according to relevance from recent literature, but also new complex indicators developed to provide simultaneous response to multiple requirements of technical, ecological, financial and social exigencies. The proposed continuous evaluation process has defined stages for both the planning and operation phase. In essence, the purpose of the evaluation is to identify the way for system sustainability, once targets fulfilled the performance level will be maintained at optimal during life cycle operation.

articleTitle: Wireless Communication Networks within Electrical Equipment
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper presents a review of wireless communication networks within electrical equipment. Following this expertise, several advantages and disadvantages of the current wireless communication methods within the electrical equipment are presented. In the final part of the paper, some aspects regarding the temperature wireless monitoring of the electrical equipment are presented using sound acoustic waves (SAW) sensors, which aim to highlight the advantages of wireless monitoring of electrical equipment. Also, in the case study, it was assessed in what matter the influences on the wireless communication network can affect the operation of the electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) integration in power grids
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Today, power systems are going through a process of transition from conventional, centrally operated power grids to smart power grids. This transition is determined both by the increasing complexity of the power grid in part through the integration of distributed energy resources and renewable energy resources, and by the need to ensure high security and continuity in operation of the grid itself. To overcome this challenge, the state of the power system at all the levels needs to be assessed in real time. Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) integration in power systems can provide the backbone for the communication infrastructure and a part of the field devices that will generate data. This paper will pursue possible points of integration of IIoT in power systems at the level of generation, transmission, and distribution of power. And also, we will point to the challenges that will be encountered during this process.

articleTitle: A Technique for Passive Ionosphere Sounding Based on Incident Wave Doppler Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The present paper proposes and tests an ionosphere sounding technique designed to evaluate the Doppler shift determined by oblique sky-wave propagation on high frequency radio waves. To this end, preexisting radio infrastructure components - consisting of a broadcast emitter and three KiwiSDR receivers - were employed, based on two software applications developed in Python and Matlab. The novelty of the proposed technique stems from the lack of dedicated sounding infrastructure, which renders the entire measurement approach low-cost. The experimental testing of the algorithm under discussion is performed through three 24-hour study scenarios that revolve around two sky wave oblique sounding channels and a direct wave propagation channel. As anticipated, the results obtained throughout the paper are in line with the theory in the field and thus prove the potential that this type of techniques have with regard to ionosphere sounding.

articleTitle: MATLAB Simulation Analysis of Harmonic Impedance in a Distribution Network in Order to optimize Passive Compensation Solutions
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Present distribution networks are undergoing a rapid increase in the level of harmonic pollution, because of the installation of an increasing number of distorting receivers, with increasing unit powers. The compensation of the reactive power in such a network, usually carried out to increase the average power factor of the consumers, can cause phenomena of amplification of the deforming regime, with negative effects on the efficiency and operational safety of the installations belonging to both the distribution operator and consumers. To avoid or mitigate these negative effects, the installation of high-power shunt capacitor banks will usually be done by associating them with or including in-absorbing passive filters or detuned filters. For a correct choice of compensation solutions, it is necessary to perform an analysis of the network in the frequency domain, to identify the parallel resonant frequencies, produced because of the presence of capacitor banks. This analysis is based on the determination of the harmonic impedances “seen” in the nodes of the network, of which the most important is the node to which the compensation installation will be connected. The harmonic impedance depends on both the characteristics of the distribution network and those of the consumers, including the compensation-filtering installations, the correctness of its determination depending on the correctness of the modeling of the circuit elements. The article presents a case study of an area of MV distribution network, carried out by modeling in the MATLAB - Simulink program environment which has in its own library a “measuring instrument” that allows the rapid determination of harmonic impedance. It is considered a stationary regime of high active and reactive load, over which an accentuated harmonic pollution is superimposed, modelled by high rms harmonic currents. Several solutions of passive current compensation on the fundamental frequency and on the most important harmonic frequencies are compared, using as main criterion the value of the total harmonic voltage distortion in the network nodes.

articleTitle: Extended Possibilities for Studying and Diagnosis of Electric Vehicles AC (Three-Phase) Charging Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: As the automotive market expands and evolve, more electrical engineering challenges occurs when it comes to study the implications of technology usage in daily life. While there is a constantly evolving frequency of presence of electric vehicles (EVs) that depends on alternating current (AC) power supplies, more specifically, on AC (three-phase) charging systems, there may be no doubts of an increased demand for extended possibilities for studying and diagnosis of these systems, while they are easy to understand, maintained and improved. For this need, it is proposed a virtual instrument that can be adopted in education, maintenance services and research, as LabVIEW software environment provides simulation capabilities among strong features for potentially monitoring of power quality in AC (three-phase) charging systems, being an excellent choice for the targeted appliances.

articleTitle: Descriptive Data Analysis of Weather Inputs for Non-Technical Losses Detection System
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Non-Technical Losses (NTL) represent losses due to electricity theft and meter malfunction and are a big problem for electrical grid and electrical sector agents. Previous studies on the subject show that electricity consumption is directly associated with temperature variations, and the non-linearity of these curves can be linked to illicit activities. Thus, the objective of this work is to perform a descriptive analysis related on consumption data of a Brazilian utility, associated with exogenous data (ambient temperature), evaluating the importance of this association on detecting and identifying possible fraudulent consumers. To be assertive, three different consumer units were identified from the inspection history, which were classified as consumer without NTL, consumer with NTL, and a suspected case. Statistical analysis of datasets was perform using Pearson Correlation Technique. In addition, a graphical analysis of possible irregularities was performed.

articleTitle: Research on optimal scaling of parts made from stainless steel material by Selective Laser Melting
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Selective Laser Melting is one of the most important 3D technologies that are used for producing metallic parts that are used in different industrial sectors (e.g. automotive). Accuracy of the realized parts is one of the most challenging issues of this technology, taking into consideration the complexity of the 3D printing process, but also particularities of this type of technology. Material's characteristics, technological parameters (laser power, scanning speed, layer thickness, hatching distance), building strategy and part orientation are only few of the most important aspects that must be considered when determining of optimal scaling of a part is considered for compensating the shrinkage that occurs in the process of 3D printing. In this paper finite element analysis and an original software application are presented, as they were used and developed by the authors to determine the optimum values of scale factors that are required to be applied for parts that are realized by Selective Laser Melting technology using Stainless Steel material in powder state form.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis a Speed and Rotor Flux Observer for Sensorless Vector Control Systems of Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2021 9th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents a new method of allocating the poles of a new adaptive rotor flux observer, designed for vector control systems with induction motors. The rotor flux is estimated by means of a full-order state observer, in which the gain matrix of the observer amplifies the error derivative between the measured and estimated stator current of the induction motor. In order to use the new rotor flux observer in sensorless vector control systems, a speed observer is designed in the paper, using a candidate Lyapunov function. The testing and evaluation of the dynamic performances of the speed and rotor flux observers are by numerical simulation in Matlab-Simulink performed.
